newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Zairean refugees cross lake into Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: Zairean refugees cross lake into Tanzania.

text.p: Zaireans fleeing fighting in the east of their country are streaming into Tanzania in rising numbers, joining Rwandans and Burundians as populations on the move, aid agencies said on Wednesday.
Dozens of the refugees had gunshot wounds, they said.
A spokesman for the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said more than 10,000 people had fled across the border and the bulk of those registered were Zaireans.
"Reports given by the newly arrived refugees indicate that thousands more are on their way," the U.N. World Food Programme added in a statement.

World Vision International, an aid organisation responsible for setting up a temporary centre for the refugees, said "about 30 of the incoming refugees from Zaire have suffered gunshot wounds, and many of the wounds are infected".

UNHCR spokesman Vincent Parker said that by Wednesday the agency had checked in 5,440 arrivals who reached Kigoma town across Lake Tanganyika, the border with Zaire; 4,066 were Zaireans, 1,259 were Burundian Hutus and 115 Rwandan Hutus.
He said local authorities had reported 5,000 others arriving by boat at villages along the lake shore.
Many fled Uvira, a Zairean town more than 100 km (60 miles) away at the north end of the lake which Tutsi rebels seized two weeks ago before spreading their offensive north.
Peaceful Tanzania already houses 650,000 Hutu refugees in camps along its borders with Burundi and Rwanda, both controlled by the Hutus' Tutsi rivals.
Lobby groups for the 1.8 million Hutu refugees say most are too scared to go home to Rwanda and Burundi.
